lines.text: Level: B1 · Topic: The Amusement Park
lines.name: Level: B1 · Topic: The Amusement Park

lines.text:
Thrills and Fun

For my birthday, my parents took me and two friends to an amusement park. We arrived when the gates opened at ten o'clock so we could make the most of the day.

The first ride we tried was the roller coaster. We waited in a queue for about twenty minutes before it was our turn. The ride started slowly as the car climbed to the top of the first hill. Then it dropped steeply and raced through loops, twists, and sharp turns. My friends screamed the whole time, but I just laughed.

After that, we went on the bumper cars. Each person drives a small electric car and tries to bump into the other cars. It was chaotic but hilarious. We also tried the spinning teacups ride, which made us quite dizzy.

At lunchtime, we stopped at a food stall and bought burgers, chips, and lemonade. The prices were expensive, but we were too hungry to care. We sat on a bench near the Ferris wheel and watched it turn slowly against the blue sky.

In the afternoon, we visited the haunted house attraction. It was dark inside, with spooky sounds, flashing lights, and actors dressed as ghosts who jumped out to scare us. One of my friends grabbed my arm so tightly that he left a mark!

Before leaving, we played some carnival games. I tried to knock down tin cans with a ball and won a small stuffed bear. My friend tried the hook-a-duck game and won a goldfish in a bag.

We left the park at six o'clock, exhausted but happy. It was the best birthday I have ever had.

lines.text: A 'theme park' has areas designed around specific themes (e.g. fantasy, adventure, movies). An 'amusement park' is more general — rides and games without a unifying theme. In practice, people often use the terms interchangeably.

lines.text: A 'funfair' or 'travelling fair' is a temporary amusement park that moves from town to town. They often appear during bank holidays or local festivals, with rides, food stalls, and game booths.
